title: Hungarian Parliament Final Preparations for May 9 Inaugural Session — Sulyok Completes Party Consultations
detail: President Tamás Sulyok completed formal consultations with all parliamentary parties on May 4, 2026 in preparation for the National Assembly's inaugural session scheduled for May 9 at 10:00 AM. Consultations covered mandate verification procedures, oath document formats, seating arrangements, and elections of parliamentary officials (Speaker, Deputy Speakers, committee chairs). All four parties represented — Tisza, Fidesz-KDNP, Mi Hazánk, and KDNP — confirmed participation. Péter Magyar is set to be elected Prime Minister by parliament and sworn in the same day — May 9, Europe Day — a date chosen by Magyar symbolically to underscore Hungary's commitment to European integration. The simultaneous swearing-in of his 16-member cabinet will also take place on May 9. Fidesz, now with 52 seats (26.1%), will take up its role as opposition for the first time since 2010, with Gergely Gulyás designated as parliamentary opposition leader.

title: Hungary Joins NATO Tiger Meet 2026 in Greece — New Gripen Livery Signals Alliance Recommitment
detail: The NATO Tiger Meet 2026 exercise began on May 4 at Araxos Air Base in Greece, with Hungary's Air Force participating alongside 11 other NATO member air forces. Hungary is displaying a new puma-themed livery on its JAS 39C Gripen jets — the first time Hungary has applied a custom livery to a Tiger Meet aircraft. The exercise (May 4–15) focuses on air-to-air combat proficiency, interoperability, and tactical exchange. Hungary's participation comes days after two additional Gripes were delivered to Kecskemét Air Base and shortly before the swearing-in of the new Magyar government, which has pledged full NATO alignment. Defense Minister-designate Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, a career military officer, is expected to attend the NATO Defense Ministers meeting in Brussels in late May to formally reaffirm Hungary's alliance commitments.
